newsitem.title: ISRAEL: FedEx to begin Israel flights next week.
newsitem.headline: FedEx to begin Israel flights next week.

text.p: The U.S. courier Federal Express Corp said on Tuesday it would begin flying cargo to and from Israel on its own planes next week.
"The inaugural flight is on June 2 and we'll fly four nights a week between Paris and Tel Aviv," spokesman Dan Arkin told Reuters.

David Bronczek, FedEx vice president for Europe, Africa and the Middle East, had said in February during a private visit to Israel that the company would begin flying its own planes in and out of Israel sometime in June.
FedEx said then it had already received approval from Israel's Airports Authority.
It had previously sent cargo to Israel on commercial carriers, including state-owned El Al Israel Airlines. Bronczek met El Al officials to discuss future cooperation.
Arkin said he did not believe the flights would cut into El Al's cargo service, for now.
"It's not exactly the same. El Al is carrying cargo, general cargo. What Federal Express is focusing on are smaller parcels and packages, what they call express," Arkin said.
"They might also take general cargo, but that is in the future."
He said the new service was a vote of confidence in Israel.
"They came to the conclusion that the market here is growing, peace is hopefully progressing...and that's why they decided," Arkin said.
